subject: Reserve lane proposal: graded GPU runway and SLA hedges — MistralBio

From: jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Subject: Reserve lane options for MistralBio — initial draft

Hi Elena / Michael,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation I’ve attached a first-pass set of dedicated reservation options that map to the milestones you outlined (pilot, beta, GA). The goal here is to give you predictable performance at each stage while keeping flexibility on cost as your inference load grows.

High-level — three graded options (attachment: reserve-lane-options_v1.pdf):
- Option A (Conserve): 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs minimum, burst to 16 during nightly batch windows — low commitment, higher burst pricing
- Option B (Balanced): 24 x A100-equivalent GPUs baseline with staged ramp to 48 over 6 months — recommended for predictable latency and a 99.5% token-SLO
- Option C (Aggressive): 64 x baseline with immediate burst capacity and reserved canary lanes for new models — best for steady high-throughput production

Key asks from you to finalize: anticipated QPS during pilot and GA, any hard budget caps for the first 12 months, whether you need private VPC deployment or hosted dedicated pool. If you’re OK with Option B as the starting point I’ll loop in Karthik and Neha for prewarm/runbook constraints and draft the commit language for the deal.

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm pilot/GA volumes by EOD Tue 11/16
2) We lock Option (A|B|C) and share engineering runbook for warm-up windows
3) We issue a DocuSign for the reserved lane and attach the SOW

Cheers,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions — Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.com]

Attachment: reserve-lane-options_v1.pdf (18 pages; capacity matrix + burn-rate)

Jordan —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the clear options. A few clarifications from our side after internal sync:
- Pilot target: ~40 concurrent users, ~200 QPS peak (inference-heavy prompts), ramp to 600 QPS at GA (target Q2).
- Budget: prefer to keep committed spend under $420k USD in the first 12 months if possible (we can trade for longer commit terms if needed).
- Compliance: we need Private deployment (VPC + KMS) for the pilot and GA. SOC2 evidence already requested — please include the hosted/private checklist.

Initial preference: leaning to Option B if you can show a stepped ramp that keeps the first 3 months under $300k while still guaranteeing latency SLOs during business hours.

Attached: Mistral_SOW_vA.docx — includes expected integration milestones and a proposed payment milestone aligned to GA.

Thanks — Elena

Thanks for the context Elena — that helps. Jordan: I sketched a graded ramp that targets Elena’s budget while keeping the token-SLOs intact. I’ve embedded the condensed option below (we’ll push a spreadsheet after this note):

Condensed options (quick view):
- Option A (12-mo floor): 8 GPUs baseline; on-demand burst for peak; est. first-year committed spend $210k — low risk, higher latency during peaks
- Option B (6-mo stair): Start at 24 GPUs for months 0–2, add 12 GPUs months 3–4, reach 48 by month 6; est. first-year committed spend $380k — fits Elena’s cap and gives predictable latency
- Option C (steady baseline): 48 GPUs baseline with 25% burst buffer; est. first-year committed spend $520k — higher cost but simplest ops

Ask: Elena, can you confirm whether the payment milestone in your SOW aligns to GA in Q2 (we'll map payment tranches to ramp phases)? If yes we’ll recommend Option B as the commercial baseline and include a 30-day canary window (revert to lower baseline if observed regressions).

Subject: Re: Reserve lane options for MistralBio — engineering notes on warm-up and minimums

Jordan / Marissa / Elena —

Quick engineering notes to make the commercial options actionable:
1) Minimum practical floor: 16 A100-equivalent GPUs if you need private VPC and want <120ms tail latency for shorter prompts; 8 GPUs will struggle once concurrency spikes above 150 QPS.
2) Staged warm-up: plan prewarm windows 2–4 hours before business-hour peaks and maintain a prefix cache to keep cost down for repeated prompt families. We can do automated prewarming tied to cron or HubSpot webhook.
3) Canary and rollback: recommend a 30-day canary where we push 10% of GA traffic to fresh model variants on reserved canary lanes; automatic fallback to baseline for errors >0.5% or latency P99 > 1.6s.
4) Quantization: for cost containment we can enable 4-bit quantization for non-sensitive models; sensitive models (PHI/PII) should remain on full precision and live in the private pool.

I’ve attached a short runbook that lists the prewarm window commands, expected boot times per GPU type, and a sample autoscale policy. If you approve Option B we’ll wire these settings into the onboarding checklist and update the SOW.

Karthik Iyer
Infra & Serving — Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Elena / Michael —

Thanks for the confirmation and the SOW. Based on the volume targets and your first-year budget envelope, our recommended path is Option B (the 6-month stair). Reasons: it meets your GA latency targets, keeps committed spend under your $420k cap when combined with a 6-month ramp, and supports private VPC + KMS as requested.

Summary of agreed items:
- Commercial: Option B, start at 24 GPUs, +12 GPUs at month 3, +12 GPUs at month 6 (baseline 48 thereafter). Commitment language will reflect step increases tied to payment tranches in your SOW.
- Engineering: Prewarm windows 2 hours before morning peak, prefix cache for repeated prompts, 30-day canary with automatic rollback rules.
- Compliance: We’ll attach SOC2 artifacts to the private deployment onboarding packet and add KMS integration notes.

Next steps (action owners):
- Marissa: update reserve-option-summary.xlsx with final pricing tiers and send commercial redline to Elena (by 11/22)
- Karthik/Neha: finalize runbook and onboarding checklist; provide an estimated date for the pilot prewarm test (by 11/24)
- Jordan: issue DocuSign for the reserve lane and the deal (DEAL-2027-112-MB) with the Option B commercial schedule (link below)
